bihar_raw_news.title: CtrlS Plans ₹10,000 Crore AI Factory in Bihar , Opens ₹400 Crore Data Centre - The420.in
bihar_raw_news.content: CtrlS Datacenters plans to invest ₹10,000 crore in a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya while opening a ₹400 crore, 12 MW data centre in Patna to serve enterprises, government institutions, hyperscalers and technology businesses. SHARE CtrlS Datacenters has signed a letter of intent with the Bihar government to invest ₹10,000 crore in a proposed 150 MW hyperscale AI factory in Bodh Gaya, while also inaugurating a ₹400 crore data centre in Patna with an initial IT load capacity of 12 MW. Contents ₹10,000 Crore AI Factory Planned in Bodh Gaya ₹400 Crore Patna Data Centre Opens With 12 MW Capacity CtrlS Plans More Than 20 Edge Data Centres The two projects expand the company’s planned infrastructure footprint in Bihar as demand for artificial intelligence computing, cloud services and data centre capacity continues to grow. The Patna facility is intended to serve enterprises, government institutions, hyperscalers and technology businesses across Bihar and eastern India. FCRF’s Chief AI Officer Certification Returns on November 14 to Prepare Future AI Leaders ₹10,000 Crore AI Factory Planned in Bodh Gaya The proposed Bodh Gaya facility represents the larger of the two investments and is planned as a 150 MW hyperscale AI factory. CtrlS has not disclosed a construction or commissioning timeline for the project. The letter of intent also does not establish when the proposed capacity will become operational. The company has not yet announced details on power arrangements, customer commitments or implementation milestones for the facility. CtrlS founder and CEO Sridhar Pinnapureddy said the investments would strengthen Bihar’s digital infrastructure and support the development of the state’s IT ecosystem. ₹400 Crore Patna Data Centre Opens With 12 MW Capacity The new Patna data centre is located in the Patliputra Industrial Area and currently provides an IT load capacity of 12 MW. The facility has scope for further expansion depending on demand and is intended to support enterprises, government institutions, hyperscalers and technology businesses. CtrlS has described the centre as being designed for disaster resilience and energy efficiency, with military-grade security. Further technical specifications were not disclosed in the available information. The new facility is expected to add data centre capacity for customers across Bihar and the wider eastern India region. CtrlS Plans More Than 20 Edge Data Centres The Bihar projects form part of CtrlS’ broader expansion strategy, under which the company plans to establish more than 20 edge data centres across Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. The company says these facilities are intended to bring computing infrastructure closer to emerging demand centres and support services requiring low latency. CtrlS, which began operations in 2007, says it operates 19 data centres across nine markets in India and plans to build more than 4.4 GW of data centre capacity by 2030. The company has not provided a detailed rollout schedule for the planned edge facilities or specified how much of its 2030 capacity target is already operational, under construction or still in planning. bihar_raw_news.title: ICAR–MGIFRI, Motihari Joins National Launch of Khet Bachao Abhiyan 2026, Unveils Rabi ...
bihar_raw_news.content: 22 October 2026, Motihari, Bihar ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar, organized a programme at its Seminar Hall to participate in the live telecast of the national launch of Khet Bachao Abhiyan (KBA) – Rabi 2026 by the Hon’ble Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare from Karnal, Haryana. During the national launch, the Union Agriculture Minister emphasized balanced and judicious fertilizer use, soil health improvement, promotion of natural farming and sustainable agricultural practices. The campaign aims to encourage soil-test-based nutrient management, organic resource recycling, crop diversification and efficient resource utilization to enhance agricultural productivity while reducing unnecessary input costs. The institute-level programme commenced with introductory remarks welcoming the Director and participants, highlighting the campaign’s objectives and significance. The institute’s action plan for the period from 22 October to 30 November 2026 was presented, outlining the formation of six multidisciplinary scientific teams to conduct village-level awareness programmes, farmer–scientist interactions, field demonstrations and provide technical advisories. Major interventions will focus on soil health management, balanced fertilization, natural farming, improved Rabi crop planning, crop diversification, conservation agriculture and prevention of crop residue burning. The detailed village-wise schedule will be finalized in coordination with the concerned KVKs and the State Agriculture Department. Dr Raghavendra Singh, Director, ICAR–MGIFRI, emphasized the importance of translating scientific innovations into practical, affordable and location-specific solutions for farmers. He highlighted the need to develop self-reliant, climate-resilient and sustainable farming systems through integrated nutrient management, natural farming, resource conservation and integration of crops, horticulture, livestock and fisheries. He encouraged all scientists and staff to actively participate in the campaign and strengthen direct outreach to farming communities. The programme concluded with a commitment to effective implementation of Khet Bachao Abhiyan – Rabi 2026, promoting healthy soils, balanced nutrient management, sustainable agricultural practices and improved farmers' livelihoods across the region. A total of 37 participants, including scientists, technical, administrative and supporting staff, along with contractual workers, attended the programme. (Source: ICAR–Mahatma Gandhi Integrated Farming Research Institute, Motihari, Bihar)

As many as 5.32 lakh voters were eligible to decide the fate of 150 candidates contesting the eight seats. According to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Darbhanga recorded the highest turnout among the Graduates’ constituencies at 8%, followed by Patna at 5.5%, Kosi at 5.14% and Tirhut at 4.81%. Among the Teachers’ constituencies, Saran recorded the highest turnout, followed by Patna. Darbhanga registered 12%, while Tirhut recorded 5.88%. The average turnout stood at 5.86% across the Graduates’ constituencies and 11.08% across the Teachers’ constituencies. Polling began at 8 am and is scheduled to continue until 4 pm. national_raw_news.title: India Counters Pakistan’s Claims on Religious Freedom at UN
national_raw_news.content: India has criticised Pakistan at the United Nations, recalling its refusal to acknowledge the bodies of its soldiers killed during the 1999 Kargil War, while raising concerns over its remarks on religious freedom and burial rights. First Secretary at India’s Permanent Mission to the UN, Bhavika Mangalanandan, said the Indian Army had buried several Pakistani soldiers with military honours and in accordance with Islamic rites. Her remarks came during a discussion on an interim report by UN Special Rapporteur on freedom of religion and belief, Nazila Ghanea, which raised concerns over alleged denial of funeral rights in Jammu and Kashmir. Mangalanandan also criticised Pakistan over the treatment of minorities, saying their numbers were declining and their rights were regularly abused. She said a country unable to ensure the safety of its own minorities had no standing to lecture India, and urged Pakistan to focus on developments in areas of Jammu and Kashmir under its illegal occupation, including Rawalakot. She further questioned the report’s approach to the burial rights of terrorists, arguing that the rights of victims of terrorism also deserved due consideration. She also accused the report of selectively highlighting human rights concerns while overlooking similar incidents in other regions, including the developed world.

national_raw_news.title: Mona Agarwal’s World Record Highlights India’s Medal Haul 5 hours ago 78
national_raw_news.content: At the Asian Para Games, India continued its medal-winning run, taking its overall tally to 104 medals, including 27 gold, 34 silver and 43 bronze. In shooting, Mona Agarwal clinched gold in the women’s 50-metre rifle three positions SH1 event, setting a new world record with a score of 357.5 to claim her second gold medal of the Games. In para-athletics, Sandeep Kumar shattered the T44 world record with a time of 52.28 seconds to win gold in the men’s 400 metres, while Ajay Kumar secured bronze in the same event. Haney also struck gold in the men’s javelin throw F37 event with a world-record effort of 60.49 metres. In para-archery, Harvinder Singh and Vijay Sundi won gold in the men’s recurve doubles event. In para-badminton, Nitesh Kumar clinched gold in the men’s singles SL3 event, while Naveen Sivakumar won gold in the men’s singles SL4 category. India also secured six silver medals across para-athletics, para-archery and para-badminton. Parmod won silver in the men’s 1,500-metre T46 event, while Pramod Bhagat finished second in the men’s singles SL3 final. Bhawna and Pooja claimed silver in women’s recurve doubles, and Nimisha Chakkungalparambil won silver in the women’s long jump T47 event with a best effort of 5.37 metres. In para-badminton, Nithya Sre Sivan won silver in women’s singles SH6, while Thulasimathi Murugesan secured silver in the women’s singles SU5 event. Thulasimathi Murugesan and Nitesh Kumar also clinched silver in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 event, losing to Indonesia’s Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani in the final. India also added a bronze medal in men’s doubles MD4 table tennis through Jehan Dorab Madan and Shubham Wadhwa.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the youth have always remained at the centre of his government’s policies and initiatives. Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi today, Mr Modi said that for the past 25 years, he has been serving the nation to the best of his ability as head of the government. Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the government has introduced the National Education Policy to align the country’s education system with the needs of a New India. He added that the policy emphasises India’s rich traditions and knowledge, imparting education in mother tongue, modern science and emerging technologies. Prime Minister Modi said that all institutions must work towards the common goals of national development and scaling the country’s pride. He stressed the need to unite society against divisive forces, promote self-reliance and involve every citizen in the resolve to build a developed India by 2047. Prime Minister said that India has brought back more than 650 stolen ancient idols and antiquities from abroad over the past twelve years. He said that the country’s cultural heritage is being restored and its cultural sites are gaining global recognition. Mr Modi highlighted that India’s cultural sites are increasingly becoming part of UNESCO World Heritage Sites. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the three-day Sammelan has brought together over nine thousand participants from India and abroad. It marks the culmination of the year-long celebrations commemorating 75 years of the Chinmaya Mission, a global spiritual movement founded by Swami Chinmayananda in 1951. The year-long celebrations began last year with the Prime Minister releasing a Tamil versification of the Bhagavad Gita. Over the decades, the Mission has expanded its work across spiritual education, cultural preservation, youth empowerment and community service.

national_raw_news.title: Satellite-Tagged Amur Falcons Return to Manipur After Migrating Across 23 Countries 1 hour ago 43
national_raw_news.content: The two satellite-tagged Amur Falcons, Apapang and Alang, have returned to Manipur after travelling across 23 countries in Asia and Africa, marking the successful completion of their nearly year-long tracking journey. In a social media post, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav said that the birds arrived in Manipur yesterday, 11 days after departing from their breeding grounds in northeastern China. He noted that the two falcons were tagged by scientists of the Wildlife Institute of India in November 2025. Akashvani Correspondent reports that the return of the Amur falcons marks the completion of a round-trip migration journey, highlighting the remarkable long-distance movements of the migratory birds. The falcons are now expected to spend two to three weeks at select stopover sites in the mountainous areas of Tamenglong district in Manipur. During this period, they will feed on termites and build up essential fat reserves for their next migratory leg. From Manipur, the birds are expected to undertake a six-day non-stop flight of nearly six thousand kilometres to Somalia, including a challenging three thousand kilometre crossing of the Arabian Sea. The annual arrival of the Amur Falcons is eagerly awaited by local communities in Manipur, who have played a significant role in protecting the migratory birds.

national_raw_news.title: CAQM reviews paddy stubble management measures in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar
national_raw_news.content: CAQM reviews paddy stubble management measures in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर CAQM reviews paddy stubble management measures in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar ANI | Updated: Oct 23, 2026 20:54 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Amritsar (Punjab) [India], October 23 (ANI): A high-level team led by the Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), visited thermal power and CBG plants, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), farm fields and a biomass plant in Ropar, Hoshiyarpur and Amritsar in the State of Punjab. The team reviewed the preparedness and took stock of various in-situ and ex-situ measures being implemented on the ground for effective paddy straw management and prevention of stubble burning incidents during the ongoing paddy harvesting season, according to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. CAQM directed the State authorities to achieve co-firing targets in thermal power plants with special focus on ensuring compliance with emission norms. During the visit to KVK, the team saw a demonstration of machinery for in-situ and ex-situ use. The team also assessed the adequacy and availability of machinery to facilitate farmers in managing paddy residue. In addition, the team reviewed the arrangements and mechanisms in place for the maximum utilisation of paddy straw in thermal power plants and biomass plants utilising paddy stubble as part of ex-situ management. With paddy harvesting gaining momentum, the Commission emphasised the need for intensified and concerted efforts by all concerned authorities to ensure that farmers have adequate access to CRM Machinery on time. The Commission directed that facilitation of farmers be maximised, with particular focus on ensuring the availability and effective deployment of machinery in accordance with the emerging requirements during the peak harvesting period. The Commission directed State Authorities to strengthen these ecosystems for paddy stubble management to minimise stubble burning incidents. The need for proactive field-level monitoring and timely resolution of operational gaps was also emphasised to ensure effective implementation of the ongoing paddy straw management interventions. national_raw_news.content: Rajnath Singh urges Army Commanders to prepare for future challenges, stresses 20-30-year strategic vision Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Rajnath Singh urges Army Commanders to prepare for future challenges, stresses 20-30-year strategic vision ANI | Updated: Oct 23, 2026 20:28 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 23 (ANI): Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has exhorted the Army Commanders to closely monitor geopolitical as well as regional developments and remain prepared for future challenges. Addressing the Army Commanders’ Conference in the national capital, he emphasised the need for a long-term strategic vision spanning the next 20-30 years, and called upon the senior leadership of the Indian Army to remain equally prepared to respond to immediate and emerging challenges. He stressed that strategies must remain dynamic and flexible, enabling timely adjustments to changing circumstances. According to the Ministry of Defence, commending the Defence Forces for adapting to evolving operational circumstances, Rajnath Singh highlighted that innovative thinking, enhanced synergy and superior coordination, complemented by advanced weaponry, contributed to the success of Operation Sindoor. "The operation sent a clear message that India would not hesitate to take necessary measures to safeguard its national interests," he said. The Defence Minister appreciated the military’s restructuring efforts, with a special focus on the use of drones and modern technology. He stressed the need to strengthen capabilities, continuously assess performance, and implement necessary improvements in line with evolving circumstances. He underscored the importance of accelerating efforts in areas such as artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, data analytics, cybersecurity, and secure communication networks. Rajnath Singh emphasised that despite the growing significance of challenges across the air, maritime, space and cyber domains, land warfare and ground forces would remain indispensable. He called for an integrated approach to modern warfare, stressing that success would depend on multi-domain capabilities and seamless coordination in joint operations. Singh acknowledged the self-reliance efforts of the defence forces, stating that India’s growing defence manufacturing capabilities are a result of concerted efforts of all stakeholders. “Amidst the changing global landscape, Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led Government is prioritising Aatmanirbharta in defence. In the financial year 2025-26, defence production surged to a record Rs 1.78 lakh crore, with defence exports reaching an all-time high of approx. Rs 38,000 crore,” he said. Referring to the ‘Year of Reforms - 2025’, Rajnath Singh stated that reform is a continuous process, the success of which depends on effective implementation. He urged the Commanders to drive these reforms forward within their respective commands and echelons, while ensuring that they translate into tangible benefits for operational capabilities. He credited the valour, discipline, preparedness and restraint of the Defence Forces, along with the dynamic leadership and diplomatic efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, for strengthening India’s global standing. He urged the Defence Forces to maintain their focus on self-reliance, effective implementation of reforms, improved manpower management, greater participation of women and an integrated approach to national security. With growing adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and generative AI applications driving demand for high-performance data centres, India's data centre capacity has grown rapidly from 375 MW in CY20 to 1,575 MW in CY26. Capacity is further projected to reach 8,000 MW by CY30, highlighting the sector's robust growth outlook. The data centre capacity pipeline growth is driven by increasing demand from cloud services, AI workloads, and digital transformation initiatives, as investments by hyperscalers and data centre operators continue to strengthen India's position as a key data centre market in the Asia-Pacific region. Accelerating Cost Efficiency Remains Key Concern As the Digital India infrastructure adds another disruptor to its plan: mega Data Centres across the national landscape, making technology sustainable and cost-effective, command the long game. The demand for power to run these current and projected facilities, and for water to cool the heat produced by data centres, currently makes headlines as economies weigh cooling technologies, cost-effectiveness, and future outlook regarding optimal usability of AI. The expected electricity demand from the growth of AI and other large-scale data centres, as per the Ministry of Power, is estimated to reach 17 GW by 2031–32, with the current capacity being about 1575 MW. However, water requirements for cooling data centres of this scale are subject to the capacity of data centres and the cooling system technology. In this regard, as per International Energy Agency (IEA) estimates, individual hyperscale data centres with a 100MW facility could require 2.5 billion litres of water annually, equivalent to the needs of approximately 80,000 people. Thus, freshwater dependence and the volume of water used under various cooling technologies become the key to making data centres cost-efficient for the future. Moreover, as cooling choice drives both power and water consumption, traditional systems like HVAC and chiller-based air-cooling systems are increasingly replaced by more efficient and relatively lower-cost alternatives such as direct-to-chip liquid cooling, adiabatic cooling, and immersion cooling. national_raw_news.content: C-DAC, Bank Of India Join Hands To Develop Indigenous Quantum Technologies For Banking Tech C-DAC, Bank Of India Join Hands To Develop Indigenous Quantum Technologies For Banking Swarajya Staff Oct 23, 2026 | Updated 04:35 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB The Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC) and public sector lender Bank of India (BOI) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to jointly explore indigenous quantum technologies and other advanced computing applications for the banking sector. According to a Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology release issued on Friday (23 October), the agreement was signed on 22 October and covers joint research, technology demonstrations, pilot projects and capacity-building initiatives. A key objective of the partnership is to develop a Quantum Ecosystem for Financial Innovation, focusing on technologies that could strengthen cybersecurity, operational resilience and decision-making in banking. The two organisations will explore quantum-inspired and quantum-safe technologies, identify potential banking applications and develop proofs of concept in secure testing environments before evaluating their feasibility for wider adoption. The collaboration will combine C-DAC's expertise in quantum computing, high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, blockchain and cybersecurity with Bank of India's banking operations and technology infrastructure. Beyond quantum technologies, the agreement also covers applications such as AI-driven fraud detection, credit and financial analytics, intelligent document processing, smart contracts, digital identity and secure data sharing. The partnership will additionally support training programmes in quantum computing, quantum security, artificial intelligence and blockchain to develop specialised technical capabilities within the financial sector. national_raw_news.title: India Steps Up Indigenous Telecom Research As C-DOT Establishes 6G, AI Centre At IIT BHU
national_raw_news.content: India Steps Up Indigenous Telecom Research As C-DOT Establishes 6G, AI Centre At IIT BHU Tech India Steps Up Indigenous Telecom Research As C-DOT Establishes 6G, AI Centre At IIT BHU Swarajya Staff Oct 23, 2026 | Updated 03:34 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Sign In Prefer Prefer Pic Via PIB The Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT), the telecom research and development arm of the Department of Telecommunications, has established its sixth Centre of Excellence (CoE) at the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), Varanasi, to advance research in next-generation communication technologies. According to a Ministry of Communications release issued on Friday (23 October), C-DOT and IIT BHU signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to facilitate collaborative research, technology development and capacity building in emerging telecommunications technologies. The centre will focus on 5G Advanced and 6G technologies , artificial intelligence-driven communication systems, quantum and post-quantum communications, cybersecurity and advanced wireless networks. Research areas will also include very large-scale Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems, integrated sensing and communication, and AI-native communication networks and devices. The collaboration aims to connect academic research with practical telecommunications requirements by bringing together researchers, faculty members, students and C-DOT technology experts. The MoU was signed in the presence of C-DOT Executive Vice President Pankaj Kumar Dalela and IIT BHU Director Professor Amit Patra. The signing ceremony was followed by the inauguration of the centre. The establishment of the CoE further expands C-DOT’s national network of Centres of Excellence to six, building on its existing collaborations with IIT Kanpur, IIT Gandhinagar, IIT Roorkee, IIT Hyderabad and IISc Bengaluru through FSID. The centres are intended to support indigenous technology development, specialised research and talent creation in India's telecommunications sector. national_raw_news.title: Comprehensive Capacity Building recommendations by Committee in MoSPI
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Towards Future-Ready Data Leaders: Comprehensive Capacity Building recommendations by Committee in MoSPI Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 11:03PM by PIB Delhi The chairman of the Committee for Reforming Capacity Building of the Indian Statistical Service (ISS), Sh. P. R. Meshram, Director General (Data Governance), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) submitted the Committee's report to Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI. This marks an important milestone toward strengthening the capacity-building framework for ISS officers. The Committee comprised senior MoSPI officers, knowledge partners, and industry experts. The Committee reviewed existing ISS training programmes, identified emerging capacity building requirements, and recommended future-oriented training aligned with the Competency Based Capacity Building (CBCB) framework of Mission Karmayogi . The framework reflects the evolving role of ISS officers in data governance, advanced analytics, emerging technologies, and evidence-based policymaking, in alignment with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. The report has been prepared through a consultative and evidence-based approach, drawing on the Statistical Training Needs Assessment, existing ISS training programmes, Mission Karmayogi frameworks, international best practices, Committee deliberations, and stakeholder consultations. The Report presents a future oriented capacity building roadmap comprising three interconnected components. The System of Today , which reviews the existing ISS training ecosystem, capability area practices, and institutional arrangements at National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) . The System of Tomorrow , which establishes a role linked, competency based capacity-building framework covering seven priority capability pillars; and Strategic Recommendations giving actionable measures to transition from current to the envisioned future system to strengthening ISS training, develop future ready competencies, and enhance NSSTA's institutional capacity. The report outlines an integrated framework comprising the ISS training ecosystem, capability pillars, and institutional architecture. It defines role expectations and assesses the competencies required for each role across functional, domain, and behavioral domains. The framework is to be anchored in the National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA) , with an emphasis on strengthening human resources, training delivery, and governance to effectively implement training reforms. Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI, complimented the Committee and the NSSTA team for their efforts and comprehensive, forward-looking recommendations. He reaffirmed the commitment to strengthening NSSTA as a pivotal training anchor for Indian Statistical Systems. Implementing these recommendations will directly fortify India's capacity-building structure, ensuring ISS officers remain fully equipped to handle next-generation data requirements and contribute toward the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 . ***** Samrat (Release ID: 2327053) Visitor Counter : 689 Read this release in: Urdu , हिन्दी Share -- words | -- min read Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Towards Future-Ready Data Leaders: Comprehensive Capacity Building recommendations by Committee in MoSPI Posted On: 22 OCT 2026 11:03PM by PIB Delhi The chairman of the Committee for Reforming Capacity Building of the Indian Statistical Service (ISS), Sh. national_raw_news.title: Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit
national_raw_news.content: Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Drinking Water and Sanitation Department organises virtual conference as follow up to Water Summit ANI | Updated: Oct 22, 2026 19:45 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, on Thursday organised the fourth virtual conference with States and Union Territories as part of a series of thematic consultations being held in follow-up to the Departmental Summit on Water 2026 held on September 1 and 2. The conference focused on strengthening convergence between Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and the 16th Finance Commission to advance source sustainability, water security and Gram Panchayat-led planning for sustainable rural drinking water service delivery. The virtual conference brought together senior officials from State PHEDs/Rural Water Supply Departments, Panchayati Raj Departments and representatives from the Ministries of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India and National Informatics Centre. State rural water supply departments, including Karnataka, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh, shared best practices and field experiences on leveraging Finance Commission grants for strengthening rural water supply systems, improving O&M arrangements, enhancing community participation and strengthening local governance mechanisms. Addressing the conference, Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, stated that with the extension of JJM 2.0, the focus now shifts from infrastructure creation to ensuring functionality, sustainability and quality service delivery. He emphasised that the true measure of success lies not merely in asset creation but in ensuring that rural households continue to receive reliable and safe drinking water through well-maintained and financially sustainable systems. Meena underlined the pivotal role of Gram Panchayats in rural water governance and noted that the 73rd Constitutional Amendment places drinking water and sanitation among the key responsibilities of local self-governments. He stressed that Gram Panchayats must take leadership in preparing comprehensive annual O&M plans, mobilising local resources, managing service delivery and ensuring accountability for water supply infrastructure created under JJM and other programmes. Referring to the 16th Finance Commission framework, he highlighted that tied grants provide a significant opportunity to strengthen the sustainability of drinking water and sanitation services at the grassroots level. He noted that of the total Rural Local Body (RLB) grants recommended by the 16th Finance Commission, a substantial share has been earmarked for water and sanitation-related activities. He emphasised that these grants should be utilised primarily for operation and maintenance, source sustainability, water quality management, service delivery improvements and strengthening local institutional capacity rather than creation of new infrastructure where existing assets require maintenance and support. The Secretary focused on three key pillars of sustainable financing for rural water supply systems such as effective utilisation of Finance Commission grants, ii. convergence with other available programmes, and iii. schemes, and progressive strengthening of user-charge collection mechanisms.
